newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ibel to cancel own shares, boosting EPS.
newsitem.headline: Ibel to cancel own shares, boosting EPS.

text.p: Belgian holding company Ibel NV said it planned to cancel 24,179 shares held as treasury stock, a move which would boost earnings per share on outstanding shares by around one percent.
In a statement published in Belgian newspapers at the weekend, Ibel said it would ask shareholders to vote on the plan at their annual general meeting on May 9.

Ibel acquired the shares as part of a policy to buy back its own shares whenever it considers their market price does not accurately reflect their intrinsic value. "This policy... will be maintained whenever the difference...is important," Ibel said.
Ibel said that during 1996 it bought 13,600 ordinary shares, at an average price of 3,529 Belgian francs each, and 10,579 reduced withholding tax shares, at an average price of 3,537 francs.
"If one counts the 53,058 shares that Ibel holds through its subsidiary Regio, the group held three percent of its own shares at December 31, 1996," Ibel said.
